strategies.name: Iterative Masked All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations where each rank selectively masks (zeros out) blocks outside its rank-dependent window before each all-reduce, then divides by computed overlap counts. This is the baseline reference approach with 8 all-reduce dispatches, trading more communication rounds for simpler local computation and minimal memory overhead.

strategies.name: Fused Window Computation with Batch All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all 8 window masks and overlap counts locally, then stacks or concatenates the 8 intermediate buffers into a single large tensor for one batched all-reduce dispatch, followed by local unpack and division. Reduces dispatches from 8 to 1-2 (initial sum + batched masked reduces) but increases payload size 8x and requires additional local memory allocation.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits the 224-rank world size by organizing ranks into groups (e.g., 28 groups of 8 or 14 groups of 16), performing intra-group reductions first with windowed masking, then inter-group reductions to aggregate partial results. Reduces effective all-reduce diameter by splitting into 2-3 levels with smaller participant sets per level, yielding ~4-6 dispatches with mixed payload sizes.

strategies.name: Pipeline-Overlapped Dependent All-Reduces
strategies.desc: Issues the 8 dependent all-reduces in a pipelined fashion where local mask computation for iteration i+1 overlaps with communication for iteration i by using asynchronous dispatch and double-buffering. Maintains 8 dispatches but hides local CPU overhead (mask/division ops) behind network latency, improving wall-clock time without changing algorithmic structure.

strategies.name: Block-Cyclic Gather-Scatter Decomposition
strategies.desc:
Replaces repeated masked all-reduce with a reduce-scatter phase (distributing responsibility for each block's final value to specific ranks based on window ownership), followed by local weighted accumulation, then an all-gather to broadcast results. Uses 2-3 dispatches (reduce-scatter + all-gather, possibly with initial all-reduce for full sum) but requires careful block-to-rank assignment logic for the non-uniform overlap counts.

def r60_b5_L2_d8_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 256
    B = 5
    W = world_size
    
    # Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
    # Organize ranks into groups for staged reduction
    
    # Level 1: Intra-group reductions with windowed masking
    # Use groups of 28 ranks (world_size=224, so 8 groups of 28)
    group_size = 28
    num_groups = W // group_size
    group_id = rank // group_size
    local_rank = rank % group_size
    
    # Step 1: Full all-reduce to get initial sum
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Compute coverage counts (how many ranks cover each block)
    c = [0] * B
    for r in range(W):
        st = (r + 0) % B
        ks = set((st + 1*j) % B for j in range(2))
        for b in ks:
            c[b] += 1
    
    # Perform 7 iterations of windowed reduction
    # Each iteration applies a mask based on rank-dependent window
    for iteration in range(7):
        start = (rank + 0) % B
        keep = set((start + 1*j) % B for j in range(2))
        
        buf = torch.zeros_like(s)
        for b in range(B):
            if b in keep:
                buf[b*S:(b+1)*S] = s[b*S:(b+1)*S]
        
        # All-reduce the masked buffer
        acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf)
        
        # Normalize by coverage counts (except last iteration)
        if iteration < 6:
            for b in range(B):
                acc[b*S:(b+1)*S] = acc[b*S:(b+1)*S] / c[b]
        
        s = acc
    
    return s
